notes: M4 heat-set inserts; bolts the cheek to the turntable plate, 4 walls, 40% infill.

Azimuth gear: module 1.5, 150 teeth on the full circle (pitch radius 112.5 mm), 80 deg cut. Bolts under the turntable plate (3 x M4 into heat-set inserts); meshes with the stepper's 15-tooth pinion. Print flat, 100% infill, 0.1 mm layers for the flanks; grease the teeth.
Sockets a 25 mm vertical pole 40 mm deep at the beam's end; two M5 x 12 down its counterbores into T-nuts in the beam's top slot. 6 walls.
Joins a vertical pole to the top pole; sockets 40 mm deep. 6 walls, 40% gyroid.
Clips the top pole and holds the 2020 stereo bar; add an M4 clamp screw each. 6 walls.
Floor of the ball path between the head plates; the shuttle slides on it. M4 heat-set inserts take screws through both head plates.
Roof over the shuttle, a column 70 mm bore up past the head plates, and a hose socket (82.5 mm) on top. Print upright, 6 walls.

Pocket for one ball (70 mm hole); the front is narrowed to 58 mm between two 1.6 mm flexure arms that hold the ball at negative elevation and let the wheels pull it out; the solid rear shuts the column while it moves 95 mm forward. Drawn retracted (pocket under the column). M4 heat-set insert in the +y side 20 mm ahead of the rear end takes the drive pin. 6 walls.
Shuttle pin to crank pin, 120 mm between 5.4 mm holes; M4 shoulder bolts (5 mm shoulder) through both. Print flat, 100% infill.

Crank, 47.5 mm throw (95 mm stroke over 180 deg of servo turn); screw it to the servo's round aluminium horn (M3 through the centre hole and two of the horn's own holes, drilled to suit). Print flat, 100% infill.

Holds the shuttle servo by its tabs outboard of the motor plate; three legs take M4 screws through the plate into heat-set inserts, and two more inserts take the servo's tab screws. Print cradle face down.

Azimuth home switch bracket on the mast plate, 45 deg round from the front. Two M3 screws through its radial slots (1.5 mm either way) into the mast plate; set it so the switch clicks with the roller in the middle of the gear sector's cam lobe. M2 pilots 6.5 mm apart for the switch: check against yours. 100% infill.

Azimuth hard stops, one each side, on the mast plate in the gap the gear sector turns in. The sector's end faces meet their pads at +-35 deg (working range +-30, home click -32). Two M4 heat-set inserts from below; screws up through the mast plate. 100% infill. Glue a 5 mm polyurethane pad on the face toward the sector.
Sleeve socket under the shelf's outlet hole: flange on the sloped shelf (M4 heat-set inserts), a vertical cup 102.5 mm across and 40 mm deep for the sleeve's top end. Print flange down, 6 walls.

Bond the hose's top end 25 mm into the socket. The funnel narrows 88 to 72 mm so a ball dropping down the sleeve cannot catch the hose's rim. The tab through the sleeve's slot takes the spring's band and keeps the collar from turning. Print funnel up, 6 walls.

Slides onto the rear lower head standoff before it is bolted in. Tie the bundle in its channel with the loop's cut length above it (manifest: cable_cut_mm); below it the wires turn +y through the motor plate's grommet hole to the motors, tachometers and servo.

Pushes into the turntable plate's centre hole from above (glue or two M3 screws). Zip-tie the bundle through its slot: the loop above it and the twisting run below it start here. The elevation actuator's lead leaves the bore on its -y wall and turns -y to the cheek's grommet (manifest elevation lead line).

An M5 x 12 and a T-nut into the cable crossbar's front slot, its head dropped into the pocket on top. Zip-tie the bundle at the bore: the run from here up to the gland twists as the head turns, so keep it free of ties.

Strap saddles over the deck-side run: 3 on the deck (two M5 x 12 each through the deck's new 5.5 mm holes, nyloc below) and 2 on the +y rear mast post's inner face (two M5 x 10 into T-nuts in its slot). Print on the ears, no support.

Hold the deck-side run 32 mm under the cable crossbar (2, M5 x 10 into a T-nut in its bottom slot) and under the axis clamp's arm (1, a zip tie round the arm through its slot), so the run can turn up into the clamp's bore on a 30 mm bend. Snap the bundle up into the ring.

Carries the azimuth stepper's StepStick driver (TMC2209 or A4988 class) in two 1x8 female headers on a scrap of 2.54 mm perfboard pushed into the windows, with a 4-way and a 2-way screw terminal (motor out, 24 V in) at the +y end and a 100 uF 35 V capacitor across 24 V at the terminal. Four M3 x 16 into the deck's M3 grid (40 x 30 mm). Set the driver's current to the manifest's stepper_amps and its microstep pins to firmware AZ_MICROSTEPS; stick its heatsink on; STEP/DIR to GPIO 14/21, EN to GND.
At y = -1300 mm (saddle 192 mm up). Two M5 x 12 button heads and T-nuts into the net beam's front slots (through the counterbores, before the gutter goes in); zip-tie the gutter in the saddle.
At y = -850 mm (saddle 168 mm up). Two M5 x 12 button heads and T-nuts into the net beam's front slots (through the counterbores, before the gutter goes in); zip-tie the gutter in the saddle.
At y = -400 mm (saddle 145 mm up). Two M5 x 12 button heads and T-nuts into the net beam's front slots (through the counterbores, before the gutter goes in); zip-tie the gutter in the saddle.
At y = +50 mm (saddle 121 mm up). Two M5 x 12 button heads and T-nuts into the net beam's front slots (through the counterbores, before the gutter goes in); zip-tie the gutter in the saddle.
At y = +500 mm (saddle 130 mm up). Two M5 x 12 button heads and T-nuts into the net beam's front slots (through the counterbores, before the gutter goes in); zip-tie the gutter in the saddle.
At y = +950 mm (saddle 153 mm up). Two M5 x 12 button heads and T-nuts into the net beam's front slots (through the counterbores, before the gutter goes in); zip-tie the gutter in the saddle.
At y = +1350 mm (saddle 174 mm up). Two M5 x 12 button heads and T-nuts into the net beam's front slots (through the counterbores, before the gutter goes in); zip-tie the gutter in the saddle.

At y = +193.5 mm, off centre so its outlet meets the lift's boot. Bolted to the net beam's front face by its rear tab (two M5 x 40 and T-nuts; the heads sit in the cavity, put them in first); the gutters' low ends rest in its saddles. Its outlet stub (72 mm bore, falling 3.6 deg) passes under the net beam and butts against the lift boot's inlet arm at the beam's rear face (glue or a strap).

Hangs under the lift base plate between the mast rails (four M5 up through the plate); the spine's foot sits in its slot. The bottom pulley's 6 mm D shaft is the gearmotor's, through the +y wall; the gearmotor's face bolts to that wall (M3 on a 31 mm circle; the wall is recessed to 0 mm there, so back it with the motor's flange). Floor 67.2 mm up; the fingers turn under it with 1.5 mm to spare. Print floor down, 4 walls; the inlet arm needs support.
Holds the three rods round the channel and bolts to the spine's +-y faces (M5 and T-nuts); the belt's up strand runs through it, clear of the fingers. The lowest one stands on the base plate.

Slides on the top of the spine (7.5 mm of travel): two M5 each side go into T-nuts in its +-y slots, which slide with the head while loose, and two M5 x 25 jack screws stand on the top rod clip and turn in captive nuts in the head to raise it and tension the belt (see the tensioner in cad/README.md). The top pulley turns on an 8 mm axle through it, 2420 mm up. Balls ride over the pulley under the hood and drop 115 deg past the top onto a 30 deg floor that falls toward the tub; the finger behind each ball pushes it down that floor. Print in two halves split on y = 300 if your printer is short of 178 mm.

One per welded cleat (32; one drawn). The 30 mm plate is the flight a ball sits on; two M3 x 12 countersunk screws go through it and the cleat (nuts on the cleat's trailing face) and its cheeks wrap the cleat's ends. The 19.5 mm pad behind lies loose on the belt's back: on the straight it takes the ball's moment 15.0 mm from the cleat (the belt presses the spine's strip with 0.60 N a ball, against 3.62 N with the cleat alone), and round a pulley the belt wraps away under it. Print on the plate's leading face, no support; 100% infill (a stalled jam puts 15 MPa in the plate).

Holds the lift gearmotor 31.0 mm out from the boot's motor recess so the jaw coupling fits between them. Screw the gearmotor's face to the end wall first (six M3 x 6 from inside, through the open end), push the coupling's motor hub on the motor's shaft through the top window (shaft fills the hub; tighten onto the flat), then slide the spacer's plug into the recess over the drive shaft's end and the spider and fix the ears with two M3 x 10 into heat-set inserts. The plug holds the near bearing's flange in. Print flange down, 5 walls, 40% infill.

Test print, before the lift boot: one bearing pocket per drawn size, cut and printed as the boot's are. Print it standing on its foot (the bores sideways, as the boot's are when it prints floor down), same printer, filament and slicer settings as the boot. Bores, radius over the bearing's 19 mm (dots over each): 1 dot -0.03, 2 dots 0.00, 3 dots 0.03, 4 dots 0.05, 5 dots 0.08, 6 dots 0.12. Press one spare F626 into each from the counterbore side in a vise (a 22 mm socket on the flange) and note a word for each: drops, slides (in snug), presses, hard (a hard squeeze) or cracks (whitens or cracks the ring). `python -m otr_cad fit-ring` with the six words takes the middle of the bores it presses into; set lift_bearing_fit_mm to that and rebuild: cad/README.md "Bearing fit test ring". The model expects the first press fit at 0.03 mm over on a printer whose sideways holes print 0.15 mm small (assumed). 4 walls, 40% infill.

Stirrer over the tub's outlet: two 115 mm arms, 12 mm tall, centred a ball's radius over the floor, 20 rpm so an arm crosses the outlet 40 times a minute. Push it on the shaft's D flat, set screw (M3 into a heat-set insert) on the flat. Print arms down, 4 walls; 230 mm long, so diagonally on a 220 mm bed.

Agitator gearmotor's mount: screw the motor's face to it first (M3 from the counterbores in its top), then bolt it up under the shelf (M4 from above into its three heat-set inserts). Print top down, 6 walls.
